story: Until 2026-12-03 (6 days), options price SENSEX to move about ±1.6%, roughly 81,943 to 84,689. In the past, the price ended inside the range priced this way 60% of the time.

For the 2026-12-03 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 88,000 (+5.6% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 80,000 (-4.0%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.

Calls and puts the same distance from the price cost about the same (gap +0.1 vol points): no strong demand for either protection or upside. Puts usually cost more than this for SENSEX: against the past year the gap is very high, so less fear is priced than usual.
SENSEX has actually been moving about 1.08% a day this past month: on the high side for it against the past year.

iv.simple: Options on SENSEX are priced for moves of about 0.89% a day. That is normal for SENSEX compared with the past year.
iv.analyst: 30-day constant-maturity ATM IV 14.2%: 63rd percentile of 1 year, 66th of all days since 2024-01-01.

vrp.simple: Options are cheap compared with how much SENSEX has actually been moving: they price 14.2% a year while the last month realised 17.1%.
vrp.analyst: IV30 - RV21 = -2.9 vol points, 15th percentile of the past year. Since 2024-01-01, IV30 was above the volatility that actually followed over the next 21 sessions on 65% of days: option sellers are usually paid a premium for carrying the risk, and the gap is what that premium looks like today.

term.simple: Near-term options on SENSEX are pricier than longer ones. The market expects something soon: an event, or stress that it thinks will pass.

skew.simple: Calls and puts the same distance from the price cost about the same (gap +0.1 vol points): no strong demand for either protection or upside. Puts usually cost more than this for SENSEX: against the past year the gap is very high, so less fear is priced than usual.
skew.analyst: 25-delta risk reversal +0.10 vol pts (front month), 97th percentile of the past year. More negative = more demand for downside insurance relative to upside.

realised.simple: SENSEX has actually been moving about 1.08% a day this past month: on the high side for it against the past year.
realised.analyst: RV21 17.1% (86th percentile of the past year), RV5 24.0%, RV63 15.3%; RV5/RV63 compression at the 86th percentile.

oi.simple: For the 2026-12-03 expiry, the biggest pile of call positions is at 88,000 (+5.6% away) and the biggest pile of put positions is at 80,000 (-4.0%). Option sellers defend these levels, so price often slows near them, but they shift as positions change.
oi.analyst: Front-expiry PCR (OI) 0.51; all-expiry OI PCR at the 3rd percentile of the past year. Today's change: calls +9,883,040, puts +3,357,320 (OI units, i.e. shares or index quantity). A high PCR in India mostly reflects put writing, so it is read as crowding, not as a signal.

futures.simple: SENSEX futures trade 468.1 points above the price itself. That premium works out to 6.0% a year, within its usual range for the past year.
futures.analyst: Near-month basis +468.1, annualised carry 6.0% (22nd percentile of the past year; its 1-year median 7.9%). Last 5 sessions (price x OI, same contracts day to day): Short covering, Long unwinding, Long build-up, Long build-up, Short build-up. Build-up labels describe what happened to positions; they do not say who is right.

move.analyst: ATM straddle / forward = 1.65% (forward 83,316.2). Scored on 720 days since 2024-01-01 against the official close on each expiry; a straddle is the market's mean absolute move, so about 57% inside is what a fair price would give.
